units.text: INT. SUBURBAN KITCHEN - NIGHT
Dark.
A storm presses on the window over the sink.
One candle on the table, a battery lantern on the counter, a fridge that has stopped humming.
MARGOT, 40s, stands at the counter slicing a loaf of bread with great care.
THEO, 20s, they/them, sits at the table with their knees drawn up.
DESMOND, 50s, Margot's husband, walks the room in his socks, trying every switch.
Nothing. Not the stove, not the porch light, not even the little green clock on the microwave.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: It's a storm, Des. It will come back.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: It's the third time this month.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Then it will come back a third time.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Can I say something and nobody does a face.
units.name: THEO

units.text: We don't do faces.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: You are doing a face right now.
units.name: THEO

units.text: That is my regular face.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Desmond laughs.
It dies in the dark.
Thunder, far off, low and patient.
Where are the girls?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Upstairs. Playing the game where they don't sleep.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Footsteps overhead.
Then on the stairs.

Then in the doorway stand THE TWINS, eight years old, identical, in matching pyjamas, each holding one end of a long silver thread that runs back into the dark of the hallway and does not appear to end.
Grandmother is here.
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: Margot lowers the knife.
Desmond turns the dead light switch again.
Theo unfolds from the chair very slowly and puts themself between the table and the door, while the candle flame leans away from the hall as if it has been told a secret.
Girls. Your grandmother died in March.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: She says she's been delayed.
units.name: THE TWINS

units.text: Desmond's phone rings on the counter.
Everyone looks at it.
He answers on speaker and the voice is a man's, flat, official, tired.
Mr. Hale? This is the Warden of the Third Gate. I'm sorry to call so late. Is Madam Odile with you yet?
units.name: WARDEN

units.text: I'm sorry, who?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: She left the Gate at six. We've been trying to reach the family since. Please don't let her cross the threshold of your kitchen until the lamps are lit. She is not, strictly speaking, herself.
units.name: WARDEN

units.text: She's not what?
units.name: THEO

units.text: The thread tightens.
Out of the dark of the hallway steps ODILE, 70s, in a wet funeral coat, her eyes two small lit lanterns.
She smiles at Margot with great tenderness.
Margot, my darling. You've cut the bread so thin. Did you know the lights go out when I'm near? I'd forgotten.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Mama.
units.name: MARGOT

units.text: Light one more candle for me. Only one more. And then we can talk about what you owe.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Nobody moves.
The candle gutters.
Rain on the glass.
The Twins hold their silver thread like a leash.
